<!-- site: execute -->

A catastrophe treaty is a function: it takes a year of the cedent's event
losses and returns what the reinsurer pays. The contract terms set its shape:
how the pieces of one storm add up, where each loss attaches, how much limit a
year has and which losses the treaty sees.

This page turns the five contracts of Larkspur Re
(`examples/data/cat_book_contracts.csv`) into code, checks the terms on small
years you can follow by hand, then runs them on the 2,000 simulated years. The
story and notation are on
[the overview](cat-0-overview.qmd). [Page 1](cat-1-loss-tables.qmd) introduces
the loss tables.

This is the R twin of the Python guide
[`cat-3-contract-terms.md`](cat-3-contract-terms.md), with the same sections,
files and numbers. `R/prospicio/tests/test-guides.R` requires each chunk to
print exactly the text under it. Lists print in the Python page's form.

## 1. The book and its contracts

The year event loss table (YELT) has one row per cedent per event piece, with a
day and an hour. `cedent_events()` builds each cedent's event set by hand with
`events_from_years()` (#594): losses per year, loss times as fractions of the
year, perils as labels.

```{r}
library(prospicio)
library(gt)

# The data files, found from the repository root (CI) or from docs/guides (Quarto).
find_data <- function(name, dir = getwd()) {
  repeat {
    path <- file.path(dir, "examples", "data", name)
    if (file.exists(path)) return(path)
    parent <- dirname(dir)
    if (identical(parent, dir)) stop("examples/data/", name, " not found", call. = FALSE)
    dir <- parent
  }
}
read_book <- function(name) {
  utils::read.csv(find_data(name), colClasses = "character", na.strings = character())
}

YELT <- utils::read.csv(find_data("cat_book_yelt.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
CONTRACTS <- read_book("cat_book_contracts.csv")
rownames(CONTRACTS) <- CONTRACTS$contract
CEDENTS <- read_book("cat_book_cedents.csv")
rownames(CEDENTS) <- CEDENTS$cedent
N_YEARS <- 2000

# One cedent's years of losses, with times (fraction of the year) and peril labels.
cedent_events <- function(cedent, perils = "all") {
  keep <- YELT$cedent == cedent
  if (perils != "all") keep <- keep & YELT$peril %in% strsplit(perils, "+", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  rows <- YELT[keep, ]
  year <- factor(rows$year, levels = seq_len(N_YEARS))
  time <- ((rows$day - 1) * 24 + rows$hour) / 8760
  ev <- events_from_years(unname(split(rows$loss, year)), times = unname(split(time, year)))
  with_labels(ev, list(peril = unlist(split(rows$peril, year), use.names = FALSE)))
}

terms <- data.frame(contract = CONTRACTS$contract, kind = CONTRACTS$kind, perils = CONTRACTS$perils,
                    share = as.numeric(CONTRACTS$share),
                    hours = ifelse(nzchar(CONTRACTS$hours), CONTRACTS$hours, "-"))
gt(terms, rowname_col = "contract") |>
  tab_header("Larkspur's five contracts", "Terms from cat_book_contracts.csv; share is Larkspur's signed line") |>
  fmt_number(columns = share, decimals = 2)
```

```text
                      kind  perils  share  hours
alder_cat_1  occurrence_xl     all   0.30     72
alder_cat_2  occurrence_xl     all   0.20     72
bracken_cat  occurrence_xl     all   0.25     72
bracken_agg   aggregate_xl   CS+FL   0.25      -
corran_qs      quota_share     all   0.10     72
```

Each row of the file becomes one `xol_layer()`. Amounts are at 100%; `share` is
Larkspur's signed line and scales every recovery. Premium is rate on line times
limit times share. Only this function reads the terms.

```{r}
num <- function(x) if (nzchar(x)) as.numeric(x) else NA_real_

contract_layer <- function(k) {
  share <- num(k$share)
  if (k$kind == "occurrence_xl") {
    limit <- num(k$limit)
    return(xol_layer(k$contract, limit, num(k$attachment), share = share,
                     premium = num(k$rate_on_line) * limit * share,
                     reinstatement_rates = rep(num(k$reinstatement_rate), as.integer(k$reinstatements))))
  }
  if (k$kind == "aggregate_xl") {
    agg_limit <- num(k$aggregate_limit)
    return(xol_layer(k$contract, Inf, 0, share = share,
                     aggregate_deductible = num(k$aggregate_deductible), aggregate_limit = agg_limit,
                     premium = num(k$rate_on_line) * agg_limit * share))
  }
  premium <- share * as.numeric(CEDENTS[k$cedent, "cat_premium"])
  with_ceding_commission(
    xol_layer(k$contract, num(k$limit), 0, share = share, aggregate_limit = num(k$aggregate_limit),
              premium = premium),
    num(k$ceding_commission)
  )
}

LAYERS <- lapply(setNames(rownames(CONTRACTS), rownames(CONTRACTS)), function(n) contract_layer(CONTRACTS[n, ]))
layers <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(LAYERS), function(name) {
  l <- LAYERS[[name]]
  data.frame(contract = name, limit = l@limit, attachment = l@attachment,
             annual_limit = l@aggregate_limit, premium = l@premium)
}))
gt(layers, rowname_col = "contract") |>
  tab_header("The five contracts as layers", "Limits and attachments at 100%, in millions; premium on Larkspur's line") |>
  cols_label(annual_limit = "annual limit") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(limit, attachment, annual_limit), decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_number(columns = premium, decimals = 3)
```

```text
             limit  attachment  annual limit  premium
alder_cat_1     40          30            80    1.800
alder_cat_2    100          70           200    1.000
bracken_cat     50          25           150    1.750
bracken_agg    Inf           0            30    0.450
corran_qs      150           0           300    3.000
```

One paid reinstatement doubles a layer's annual limit. The aggregate cover has
no occurrence limit.

## 2. What counts as one loss: the hours clause

A storm can enter the loss table in pieces (a windstorm over two days, hail
cells). The hours clause sets how many hours of losses make one **occurrence**.
Under 40 xs 30, two pieces of 25 recover nothing separately and 20 together.

**The rule on this track.** `hours_clause()` starts a window at a year's first
piece and joins every piece within that many hours of it, then starts the next
window at the next piece. It groups all perils together, with the one `hours`
value of the contracts file. Both choices are simplifications.

A real clause usually lets the cedent choose where each window starts, so a
fixed window can understate recoveries. Many clauses also set a window per
peril, longer for flood (often 168 hours) than for windstorm. The chunks below
test the per-peril rule on this book.

```{r}
# Numbers and vectors printed as Python prints them, so both pages print the same.
py_num <- function(v) {
  v <- as.character(round(v, 4))
  if (grepl("[.e]", v)) v else paste0(v, ".0")
}
py_list <- function(x) {
  if (!length(x)) return("[]")
  if (is.character(x)) return(paste0("['", paste(x, collapse = "', '"), "']"))
  paste0("[", paste(vapply(x, py_num, character(1)), collapse = ", "), "]")
}

alder <- cedent_events("alder")
alder_72 <- hours_clause(alder, 72)
cat("labels before", py_list(alder@label_dims), " after", py_list(alder_72@label_dims), "\n")

ceded_mean <- function(layer, events) {
  res <- aggregate(apply_tower(reinsurance_tower(list(layer)), events), keep = c("kind", "layer"))
  mean(marginal(res, list(kind = "ceded", layer = layer@name)))
}

cat_1 <- LAYERS[["alder_cat_1"]]
```

```text
labels before ['peril']  after []
```

Grouping removes the labels, because an occurrence of pieces of two perils has
no single peril. To group by peril, group each peril separately, label it again
and merge with `merge_event_sets()`. The merged set keeps the labels and orders
each year's occurrences in time. Page 4 reuses this helper.

```{r}
grouped_by_peril <- function(cedent, hours) {
  out <- NULL
  for (p in c("WS", "EQ", "FL", "CS")) {
    g <- hours_clause(cedent_events(cedent, p), hours)
    g <- with_labels(g, list(peril = rep(p, sum(event_counts(g)))))
    out <- if (is.null(out)) g else merge_event_sets(out, g)
  }
  out
}

alder_72p <- grouped_by_peril("alder", 72)
rules <- list(alder, alder_72, alder_72p)
grouping <- data.frame(rule = c("no clause", "72 hours, all perils", "72 hours, by peril"),
                       occurrences = vapply(rules, function(e) sum(event_counts(e)), numeric(1)),
                       expected_loss = vapply(rules, function(e) ceded_mean(cat_1, e), numeric(1)))
gt(grouping, rowname_col = "rule") |>
  tab_header("alder_cat_1 under three grouping rules", "Expected loss in millions on Larkspur's line") |>
  cols_label(expected_loss = "expected loss") |>
  fmt_number(columns = occurrences, decimals = 0, use_seps = FALSE) |>
  fmt_number(columns = expected_loss, decimals = 4)
```

```text
                      occurrences  expected loss
no clause                    5391         0.7778
72 hours, all perils         4238         0.8230
72 hours, by peril           4275         0.8229
```

Grouping raises the expected loss by about 6%. Grouping by peril adds a few
occurrences (pieces of different perils in the same 72 hours no longer join)
and barely moves it, so the track prices with the single all-perils
clause and groups by peril only where it needs the labels.

## 3. Alder's layers: occurrence excess of loss with reinstatements

An occurrence `x` recovers `min(max(x - a, 0), l)` from a layer `l xs a`.
Recoveries add up over the year until the annual limit, `l` times one plus the
reinstatements, is used. Paid reinstatements cost the cedent more premium; page
5 prices them.

`ceded_by_event()` shows the order. Take `alder_cat_1` (40 xs 30, 30%, one
reinstatement, so 80 of annual limit) and four occurrences: one below the
attachment, one through the top, two in the middle.

```{r}
year <- c(28, 110, 64, 95)
line <- as.numeric(CONTRACTS["alder_cat_1", "share"])
left <- cat_1@aggregate_limit
recs <- ceded_by_event(cat_1, year)
left_after <- numeric(length(year))
for (i in seq_along(year)) {
  left <- left - recs[i] / line
  left_after[i] <- max(left, 0)
}
cat(sprintf("year: %.2f\n", ceded(cat_1, year)))
steps <- data.frame(loss = sprintf("%.0f", year), at_100 = recs / line, limit_left = left_after,
                    line = recs)
gt(steps, rowname_col = "loss") |>
  tab_header("alder_cat_1 on a year of four occurrences", "Amounts in millions, in time order") |>
  cols_label(at_100 = "at 100%", limit_left = "limit left", line = "Larkspur's line") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(at_100, limit_left), decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_number(columns = line, decimals = 2)
```

```text
year: 24.00
     at 100%  limit left  Larkspur's line
28       0.0        80.0             0.00
110     40.0        40.0            12.00
64      34.0         6.0            10.20
95       6.0         0.0             1.80
```

Alone, the 95 recovers 40, but only 6 of the annual limit remains: late
occurrences get what is left, so order matters. The book's years are in time
order (the file lists pieces by `slot`). In the figure, the first bar of each
event is what the layer pays at 100%, and the second is the annual limit left.
The 28 pays nothing and the 95 gets only the 6 that remain.

```{r}
#| label: limit-figure
library(ggplot2, exclude = "layer")   # keeps prospicio's layer()
paid <- ceded_by_event(cat_1, year) / line
remaining <- pmax(cat_1@aggregate_limit - cumsum(paid), 0)
occurrences <- factor(paste("loss", year), levels = paste("loss", year))
bars <- data.frame(occurrence = rep(occurrences, 2),
                   what = factor(rep(c("paid by the layer (100%)", "annual limit left"), each = length(year)),
                                 levels = c("paid by the layer (100%)", "annual limit left")),
                   amount = c(paid, remaining))
ggplot(bars, aes(occurrence, amount, fill = what)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = "occurrence, in time order", y = "amount at 100% (millions)", fill = NULL,
       title = "alder_cat_1, 40 xs 30: the annual limit runs out") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## 4. Corran's quota share: an event limit and an annual limit

A plain quota share cedes a fixed share of every loss. A cat quota share
adds an event limit and an annual limit. `corran_qs` cedes 10% with an event
limit of 150 and an annual limit of 300 at 100%: a layer 150 xs 0 at a 10% share
with an annual limit of 300. In a year of 200 and 120, the event limit caps the
first event at 150, so the cover pays 10% of 270. `quota_share()` has no limits
and pays 10% of 320.

```{r}
qs <- LAYERS[["corran_qs"]]
cat(py_num(ceded(qs, c(200, 120))), py_list(ceded_by_event(qs, c(200, 120))), "\n")
cat(py_num(ceded(quota_share("uncapped", 0.1), c(200, 120))), "\n")
```

```text
27.0 [15.0, 12.0]
32.0
```

## 5. Bracken's aggregate cover, and the losses it sees

The **subject losses** of a contract are the cedent's losses of its perils,
grouped by its hours clause, before its terms. `bracken_agg` covers only
convective storm and flood, so remove the other perils first:
`cedent_events("bracken", "CS+FL")` (#584).

A split by label cannot do this, because it comes after the cession. Take an
earthquake of 25, then a windstorm of 30, under 20 xs 10 with an annual limit of
20. The earthquake recovers 15 and leaves 5 for the windstorm. A windstorm-only
treaty pays 20 for it.

```{r}
year <- with_labels(events_from_years(list(c(25, 30)), times = list(c(0.1, 0.2))),
                    list(peril = c("EQ", "WS")))
small <- xol_layer("20 xs 10", 20, 10, aggregate_limit = 20)
split_res <- apply_tower(reinsurance_tower(list(small)), year)
for (peril in c("EQ", "WS")) {
  m <- mean(marginal(split_res, list(kind = "ceded", layer = "20 xs 10", peril = peril)))
  cat(sprintf("%s share of the all-perils recovery %.1f\n", peril, m))
}
ws_only <- apply_tower(reinsurance_tower(list(small)), events_from_years(list(30), times = list(0.2)))
ws_only <- aggregate(ws_only, keep = c("kind", "layer"))
cat(sprintf("WS under a windstorm-only treaty %.1f\n",
            mean(marginal(ws_only, list(kind = "ceded", layer = "20 xs 10")))))
```

```text
EQ share of the all-perils recovery 15.0
WS share of the all-perils recovery 5.0
WS under a windstorm-only treaty 20.0
```

A label split gives the windstorm's part of this treaty's recovery, not what a
windstorm treaty pays.

An aggregate cover pays `share * min(max(S - AD, 0), AL)` on the annual total
`S`, with aggregate deductible `AD` and limit `AL`. In prospicio it is a layer
with an infinite occurrence limit, no attachment and the annual terms.
`bracken_agg` is 30 xs 40 in the aggregate at 25%. A year of 10, 20 and 25
totals 55, so the cover pays a quarter of 15.

```{r}
agg <- LAYERS[["bracken_agg"]]
cat(py_num(ceded(agg, c(10, 20, 25))), "\n")
agg_pro_rata <- xol_layer("bracken_agg", Inf, 0, share = 0.25, aggregate_deductible = 40,
                          aggregate_limit = 30, allocation = "pro_rata")
split <- data.frame(loss = c("10", "20", "25"),
                    event_order = ceded_by_event(agg, c(10, 20, 25)),
                    pro_rata = ceded_by_event(agg_pro_rata, c(10, 20, 25)))
gt(split, rowname_col = "loss") |>
  tab_header("bracken_agg on a year of 10, 20 and 25", "Recovery by event, in millions on Larkspur's line") |>
  cols_label(event_order = "event order", pro_rata = "pro rata") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(event_order, pro_rata), decimals = 4)
```

```text
3.75
    event order  pro rata
10       0.0000    0.6818
20       0.0000    1.3636
25       3.7500    1.7045
```

The annual value is the same; the split by event differs. In event order the
deductible takes the first losses and the third event gets all the recovery.
`allocation = "pro_rata"` scales every event by the same factor. The split
matters only when a later step reads events, such as an inuring stage (page 4).

On the book, the cover sees only Bracken's convective storm and flood losses.

```{r}
bracken_csfl <- cedent_events("bracken", "CS+FL")
annual <- total(total(bracken_csfl))@draws
largest <- total(annual_maxima(bracken_csfl))@draws
past <- which(annual > 40)
cat(sprintf("mean CS+FL annual loss %.4f\n", sum(annual) / N_YEARS))
cat(sprintf("years past the deductible %.4f, years that use the whole limit %.4f\n",
            length(past) / N_YEARS, sum(annual >= 70) / N_YEARS))
cat(sprintf("of the %d years past the deductible, %d have one loss above 40\n",
            length(past), sum(largest[past] > 40)))
cat(sprintf("bracken_agg expected loss %.4f, premium %.4f\n", ceded_mean(agg, bracken_csfl), agg@premium))
```

```text
mean CS+FL annual loss 7.1642
years past the deductible 0.0325, years that use the whole limit 0.0130
of the 65 years past the deductible, 52 have one loss above 40
bracken_agg expected loss 0.1621, premium 0.4500
```

The cover attaches in about one year in thirty. It does not cap one event's
contribution, so a single large flood or storm outbreak is the usual trigger: in
52 of the 65 years past the deductible, one loss alone is above it. For
frequency protection, add an each-and-every-loss cap on each event's
contribution.

## 6. All five contracts on the book

Each contract runs on its own perils and hours clause. The loss ratio is
expected ceded loss over upfront premium, before reinstatement premium and
commissions.

```{r}
subject <- function(k) {
  e <- cedent_events(k$cedent, k$perils)
  if (nzchar(k$hours)) hours_clause(e, as.numeric(k$hours)) else e
}

```

```{r}
#| label: contracts-table
contracts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(rownames(CONTRACTS), function(name) {
  l <- LAYERS[[name]]
  data.frame(contract = name,
             expected_loss = ceded_mean(l, subject(CONTRACTS[name, ])), premium = l@premium)
}))
contracts$loss_ratio <- contracts$expected_loss / contracts$premium
gt(contracts, rowname_col = "contract") |>
  tab_header("Larkspur's five contracts on the 2,000 simulated years",
             "Amounts in millions, on Larkspur's line, before reinstatement premium and commissions") |>
  cols_label(expected_loss = "expected loss", loss_ratio = "loss ratio") |>
  fmt_number(columns = expected_loss, decimals = 4) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(premium, loss_ratio), decimals = 3)
```

```text
             expected loss  premium  loss ratio
alder_cat_1         0.8230    1.800       0.457
alder_cat_2         0.4163    1.000       0.416
bracken_cat         0.6847    1.750       0.391
bracken_agg         0.1621    0.450       0.360
corran_qs           1.2025    3.000       0.401
```

```{r}
#| label: contracts-figure
shown <- data.frame(contract = factor(rep(contracts$contract, 2), levels = rev(contracts$contract)),
                    what = factor(rep(c("premium", "expected loss"), each = nrow(contracts)),
                                  levels = c("premium", "expected loss")),
                    amount = c(contracts$premium, contracts$expected_loss))
ggplot(shown, aes(amount, contract)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = what), position = position_dodge2(reverse = TRUE)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("premium" = "grey75", "expected loss" = scales::hue_pal()(2)[1])) +
  labs(x = "millions, on Larkspur's line", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "Expected loss against premium, by contract") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## 7. The contract year

A treaty covers losses that occur in a period (losses occurring) or losses on
policies written in a period (risks attaching). prospicio models this with a
`timeline()` of accident months, an exposure matrix of how much of each month
each underwriting year carries, and a tower with a cover basis
(`with_cover_basis()`).

Under losses occurring, contract years start at month 0 of the timeline. Trap:
an 18-month timeline with one underwriting year keeps an event in month 3 and
silently drops an event in month 16.

```{r}
ev <- events_from_years(list(c(100, 80)), times = list(c(3 / 18, 16.2 / 18)))
lo <- with_cover_basis(reinsurance_tower(list(xol_layer("XL", 50, 20))), "losses_occurring")
res <- apply_tower_timeline(lo, timeline(ev, 18), matrix(1, nrow = 1, ncol = 18))
keys <- res@keys
cat("[", paste(sprintf("('%s', '%s', %s)", keys$kind, keys$layer, keys$year), collapse = ", "), "]\n",
    sep = "")
cat(sprintf("gross seen %.1f\n", mean(marginal(res, list(kind = "gross", layer = "ground_up", year = 1)))))
```

```text
[('gross', 'ground_up', 1), ('ceded', 'XL', 1), ('net', 'retained', 1)]
gross seen 100.0
```

The 80 in month 16 is in no contract year, and prospicio gives no warning
(#586). Here the simulated years are already contract years.

## 8. Surplus and per-risk covers

A surplus treaty cedes each risk in proportion to the amount by which its sum
insured exceeds a retention. A per-risk excess of loss attaches on each risk,
not each event. Both need losses by risk, which a catastrophe event table does
not have. [`reinsurance-price.md`](reinsurance-price.md), a
Python guide, shows `surplus_treaty()` and risk profiles.

## In Python

The Python guide, [cat-3-contract-terms.md](cat-3-contract-terms.md), builds
the same contracts with `Layer`, `Layer.quota_share`,
`Layer.with_ceding_commission`, `EventSet.grouped`, `EventSet.merge`,
`Layer.ceded_by_event`, `Tower.apply`, `Timeline` and `Tower.apply_timeline`.
